title.narrative: CSF_Support till nationella och lokala policyer för klimatförändringar
CSF_Support to National and local Climate Change Policies

description.narrative:
Syftet med insatsen är att stödja insatser för att minska avskogningen och växthusgasutsläppen – till år 2030 och 2050. För att uppnå detta huvudmål har tre specifika mål fastställts:
- Mål 1: Att stödja utformningen av en strategi för minskning och begränsning av avskogning på nationell nivå, baserad på utarbetandet av en aktionsplan för att uppnå målen för skogsbruks- och jordbrukssektorerna som fastställts i NDCs för den plurinationella staten Bolivia 2021-2030.
- Mål 2: Att analysera, bedöma och utforma minst en finansiell mekanism för att förbättra genereringen av egna inkomster för den nationella myndigheten för skyddade områden - SERNAP
-Mål 3: Att analysera de ekonomiska konsekvenserna av genomförandet av de åtgärder som identifierats i den regionala strategi för klimatförändringar som utarbetats av departementsregeringen i Santa Cruz, i den så kallade Departmentally Determined Contributions (DDC), och identifiera i) deras kostnadseffektivitet, ii) kostnaden för deras genomförande, iii) deras inverkan på makroekonomiska resultat på departamentsnivå, iv) Jämförelse av den makroekonomiska prognosen – baserad på ett grundscenario (utan DDC).
Tidsramen för insatsen är två och ett halvt år med en aktivitetsperiod på två år (24 månader). Insatsen har en beräknad kostnad på cirka 7 998 480 kronor.

The aim of the intervention is to support efforts to reduce deforestation and GHG-emissions - towards the years 2030 and 2050.
To achieve this main objective, three specific objectives have been established:
- Objective 1: To support the design of a Deforestation Reduction and Mitigation Strategy at the national level, based on the development of a Roadmap to achieve the goals of the Forestry and Agricultural sectors established in the NDC of the Plurinational State of Bolivia 2021-2030
- Objective 2: To analyse, assess and design at least one financial mechanism to improve the generation of own income for the National Authority of Protected Areas - SERNAP
-Objective 3: To analyse the economic impact associated with the implementation of the measures identified in the Departmental Climate Change Strategy developed by the Departmental Government of Santa Cruz, hereinafter called Departmentally Determined Contributions (DDC), identifying i) their cost-efficiency, ii) the cost associated with their implementation, iii) their impact on macroeconomic performance at the departmental level, and iv) the comparison of the macroeconomic projection - based on a baseline scenario (without EDCC).
The timeframe of the intervention is two and half years with an activity period of two years (24 months). The contribution has an estimated cost of about SEK 7 998 480 .

This proposal seeks to contribute to the national and departmental public policies to combat climate change, based on a joint collaboration with academia, civil society and the public sector. The aim is to support efforts to reduce deforestation and CO2eq emissions up to the years 2030 and 2050. To achieve this main objective, three specific objectives have been established: - Objective 1: To support the design of a Deforestation Reduction and Mitigation Strategy at the national level, based on the generation of a Roadmap to achieve the goals of the Forestry and Agricultural sectors established in the NDC of the Plurinational State of Bolivia 2021-2030 - Objective 2: To analyse, assess and design at least one financial mechanism to improve the generation of own income for the National Authority of Protected Areas SERNAP -Objective 3: To analyse the economic impact associated with the implementation of the measures identified in the Climate Change Departmental Strategy developed by the Departmental Government of Santa Cruz, hereinafter called Departmentally Determined Contributions (CDD), identifying i) their cost-efficiency, ii) the cost associated with their implementation, iii) their impact on macroeconomic performance at the departmental, and iv) the comparison of the macroeconomic projection with respect to a baseline scenario (without EDCC).
At the end of the intervention is expected: -The establishment of a Roadmap to reduce and mitigate deforestation in Bolivia, in such a way that it is viable and applicable within the terms established in the updated NDC (and its goals until the year 2030), outlining actions and goals that contribute to achieving the sectoral measures defined for the Forestry and Agricultural sectors. - The design of at least one new financing mechanism for SERNPAC, based on reliable technical information, and the roadmap for its implementation and inclusion in SERNAPs Collection System. - A report that will contain the results of the model simulations that show the macroeconomic effects and the financial needs of the implementation of key climate change mitigation policies in the department of Santa Cruz (aimed at reducing CO2eq emissions in accordance with the CDDs, Bolivian´s NDC and the objectives of CO2eq emissions by 2050). In a complementary and descriptive way, it is planned to identify and analyse the gender implications that the proposed policies may have.

title.narrative: First Amendment between CSF and Sida to Support National and Local Climate Change Policies
Grant Agreement with CSF regarding support to National and Local CC Policies
Decision on Contribution Support to Climate Change Policies

description.narrative:
The main resultas achieved by components are as follow.
Component 1: National Deforestation Reduction Strategy. The analysis of the causes of deforestation and possible solutions was completed during the first quarter of 2024. This process has included: i) literature review and information collection to analyze the causes and trends of deforestation in Bolivia, ii) the review of experiences internationalization on effective policies to reduce deforestation, iii) the identification of conservation and comprehensive management of the forest, and iv) the key regulatory changes necessary that could significantly contribute to reducing deforestation in the country, among others. Once the analysis process was completed, and once a draft strategy was available, validation workshops have been held and a final draft of the whole strategy was delivered to the Mother Land Plurinational Authority "APMT" on April, incorporating all the feedbacks and comments from the validation workshops. Subsequently, this draft has been again socialized with the governmental bodies of the forest round table. Currently, CSF is receiving additional recommendations, which are being incorporated into the document. It is expected that the final version of the strategy will be presented by the APMT on June/July , in an official event.
Component 2: Mechanisms to generate own income for SERNAP (this component includes three subcomponents). 2.1 Environmental Passport. The design phase of the environmental passport has been completed. This involved carrying out an economic study on availability of payment, which reached more than 1000 observations at the national level. Initially, the launch of the passport for June, but considering all the actions that must be completed prior to launch, it was decided to move the date until September. Currently, CSF is supporting three key elements to be able to launch the instruments: i) the design of the Ministerial Resolution, ii) the definition of the body that will administer the resources, and iii) the preparation of a web platform that serves to manage the passport from SERNAP.
2.2 Proposal for a Supreme Decree to protect supply and recharge waters in protected areas The draft supreme decree has been worked in coordination with the SERNAP legal team and currently is in the process of review and approval by the Ministry of Environment and Water. (MMAyA). CSF has supported with all the technical information and background needed to justify the necessity to protect the water resource. 2.3 Implementation of SISCO rates for national and foreign tourists in the PNANMI Cotapata. CSF has supported the design of the financial mechanism for the Cotapata Protected Area. The application of surveys, data processing and analysis was completed. With this information, and based on the results of econometric exercises, a rate recommendations for SISCO, both for national and foreign visitors has been suggested to SERNAP. Work was also carried out on a SISCO implementation strategy. Currently, CSF is supporting the implementation process by presenting the results of the study in different workshops and events, including presentations in the area to the management committee, operators and SERNAP officials. It is expected its official approval before the end of the activity period.
Component 3: Economic Impact Study of the Climate Change Strategy of Santa Cruz. The analysis was completed, which includes a baseline and the estimates of the GHG potential emissions reduction by the different economic sectors and for each of the measures analyzed. It also includes the capital and operating costs of the strategy measures proposed by the Government of Santa Cruz. The macroeconomic model has also been developed and forecast the behavior of the economy and GHG emissions for the period 2024- 2050.
An additional contribution of this project was the support to the Government of Santa Cruz in the review and adjustments of the mitigation measures that are described in the Department's climate strategy and policy. That review allowed the incorporation of a measure on reducing deforestation (which was absent), thus a measures aimed at promoting more sustainable production systems, especially for the livestock sector. The results of the study were presented in the GCF Task Force meeting, held in the city of Santa Cruz on Thursday, April 25. Currently CSF is the process of the final adjustments to the document which will possibly be delivered to the Governor, in an official ceremony at the end of June.
Component 4: Benefit Sharing Mechanism "BSM"(LEAF Process). The design of the BSM was carried out through a diagnostic analysis of historical deforestation and its causes in the jurisdictions of Pando and Charagua, the review of experiences in the region, a wide consultation process with national and international experts, as well as consultations with local actors in both jurisdictions. Based on the results, the BSM proposal was made considering the disparities in both territories to establish an effective incentive system in each jurisdiction This proposal also addresses the conditions and regulatory procedures for its implementation. The design stage was concluded and the first draft of the BSM was presented to the Vice Presidency on April 12th. BSM's proposal was very well received. As a next step, it is expected to present the proposal in both jurisdictions, through socialization workshops.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
